title: OpenBench Index
subtitle: Aggregated benchmark scores of open-weight LLMs across many benchmark suites.

columnCards.name: VRAM Requirements
columnCards.description: Single-model inference VRAM at FP16, INT8 and INT4 precision, estimated by Spheron's per-model GPU recommender. The GPU filter keeps a model when its smallest variant fits the selected budget after the reserve.

coding_index.name: OpenBench Coding Index
coding_index.description: This site's own coding composite, derived from the coding benchmarks in this table by derive_coding_index.py. Each benchmark becomes a percentile rank, averaged with per-benchmark reliability weights; missing scores are imputed toward the median. Whole index points, median near 50,000, relative to the models currently in the table.

aa_intelligence_index.name: AA Intelligence Index
aa_intelligence_index.description: Artificial Analysis composite index of overall model capability; v4.1 since 2026-06-15. Weighted average of nine evaluations in four categories: Agents 34%, Coding 24%, Scientific Reasoning 24% and General 18%. Scored on Artificial Analysis' index scale rather than as a percentage.

aa_coding_index.name: AA Coding Index
aa_coding_index.description: Artificial Analysis composite index for coding: an equal-weighted average of Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SciCode, on the same index scale as the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index rather than as a percentage.

swe_bench_verified.name: SWE-bench Verified
swe_bench_verified.description: Human-validated subset of SWE-bench for fixing real GitHub issues; solutions are judged by running unit tests.

swe_bench_pro.name: SWE-bench Pro
swe_bench_pro.description: Successor to SWE-bench Verified for realistic software engineering tasks; spans Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Go, and is designed to be more contamination-resistant and industry-relevant.

swe_atlas_rf.name: SWE Atlas: Refactoring
swe_atlas_rf.description: Refactoring track of Scale AI's SWE Atlas suite: restructure production code to improve readability and maintainability while preserving behavior; 70 tasks graded by programmatic test validation plus rubric assessment. Metric is Task Resolve Rate (% of tasks passing all rubric items).

swe_atlas_tw.name: SWE Atlas: Test Writing
swe_atlas_tw.description: Test Writing track of Scale AI's SWE Atlas suite: write meaningful tests that exercise real functionality and raise coverage; 90 tasks graded by manifest check, mutation testing and rubric assessment. Metric is Task Resolve Rate (% of tasks passing all rubric items).

swe_atlas_qna.name: SWE Atlas: Codebase Q&A
swe_atlas_qna.description: Codebase Q&A track of Scale AI's SWE Atlas suite: deep code-comprehension tasks such as tracing execution paths, multi-file reasoning and answering technical questions, with no code changes required; 124 tasks across 11 open-source repos in Go, Python, C and TypeScript. Metric is Task Resolve Rate (% of tasks passing all rubric items).

deepswe.name: DeepSWE
deepswe.description: Benchmark measuring frontier coding agents on original, long-horizon and hand-written software engineering tasks on active open-source repositories; Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go and Rust.

frontierswe.name: FrontierSWE
frontierswe.description: Benchmarking software engineering skill at the edge of human ability; hand-crafted tasks, scored by Dominance (pairwise win-rate %) and average rank.

frontiercode.name: FrontierCode
frontiercode.description: Cognition's benchmark of exceptionally hard, hand-crafted software engineering tasks at the frontier of model capability; contamination-resistant and unsaturated (top models score below 30%).

swe_marathon.name: SWE-Marathon
swe_marathon.description: Ultra-long-horizon agentic software engineering: 20 multi-hour tasks (library reproductions, full-stack product clones, ML engineering), each with an executable environment, a human-written reference solution and a multi-layer verification suite; logged attempts average 27.2M tokens per task.

swe_rebench.name: SWE-Rebench
swe_rebench.description: A continuously updated, decontaminated benchmark for evaluating software-engineering LLMs on real-world coding tasks under a standardized evaluation setup.

livecodebench.name: LiveCodeBench
livecodebench.description: Contamination-resistant coding benchmark that continuously collects new problems; evaluates code generation, self-repair, code execution, and test output prediction.

scicode.name: SciCode
scicode.description: Scientific coding benchmark evaluating code generation and problem solving in scientific domains.

terminal_bench_2_1.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
terminal_bench_2_1.description: Terminal-Bench 2.1 is a collection of tasks and an evaluation harness to help agent makers quantify their agents' terminal mastery.

terminal_bench_2_0.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
terminal_bench_2_0.description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 is a collection of tasks and an evaluation harness to help agent makers quantify their agents' terminal mastery.

terminal_bench_hard.name: Terminal-Bench Hard
terminal_bench_hard.description: Hard subset of Terminal-Bench tasks; benchmark of real terminal tasks in sandboxed environments with test scripts.

toolathlon.name: Toolathlon-Verified
toolathlon.description: The Tool Decathlon: long-horizon agentic tool use across 32 real MCP servers plus 7 local toolkits, with 108 tasks averaging around 20 interaction steps. Grading is execution-based on the final state of the applications. Scores are the Toolathlon-Verified series, not comparable with earlier Toolathlon numbers. Metric is Pass@1.

tau3_bench_banking.name: τ³-Bench Banking
tau3_bench_banking.description: Banking domain of τ³-Bench, as run by Artificial Analysis. τ³ adds a knowledge-retrieval layer to the dual-control τ² setup: action tools are hidden in knowledge-base documents, so the agent must search for them and unlock them with meta-tools before calling. Metric is task success rate.

tau2_bench_telecom.name: τ²-Bench Telecom
tau2_bench_telecom.description: Dual-control conversational agent benchmark where both agent and user use tools in a shared environment; includes a compositional task generator; Telecom domain.

gdpval_aa.name: GDPval-AA v2
gdpval_aa.description: Artificial Analysis' v2 evaluation framework over OpenAI's GDPval dataset: real work deliverables — documents, slides, spreadsheets — for 44 occupations across 9 industries, authored with experienced professionals. Scored by pairwise LLM-judge comparisons aggregated into an Elo in which 1000 is human expert performance.

browsecomp.name: BrowseComp
browsecomp.description: Browsing benchmark with 1,266 challenging short-answer questions designed to be hard to find but easy to verify.

aa_omniscience.name: AA-Omniscience
aa_omniscience.description: Artificial Analysis' knowledge and hallucination benchmark: 6,000 questions over 42 economically relevant topics in six domains. The Omniscience Index is a bounded −100 to 100 score that rewards correct recall, penalises confident wrong answers and credits abstention; 0 means as often right as wrong.

aa_omniscience_hallucination.name: AA-Omniscience Hallucination Rate
aa_omniscience_hallucination.description: Companion metric to AA-Omniscience: of all responses that were not correct, the share that were confident wrong answers rather than partial answers or abstentions — incorrect / (incorrect + partial + not attempted). It measures what a model does when it does not know, so lower is better.

aa_lcr.name: AA-LCR
aa_lcr.description: Artificial Analysis Long Context Reasoning: 100 open-answer questions over real documents of 10k-100k tokens. Each needs multi-step reasoning that synthesises facts scattered across the text rather than a single lookup. Graded pass/fail by an LLM judge; metric is the average pass rate.

critpt.name: CritPt
critpt.description: Complex Research using Integrated Thinking - Physics Test ("critical point"): 70 research-level physics challenges written by 50+ active researchers across 11 subfields, decomposed into 190 machine-verifiable checkpoint tasks. Deeply unsaturated: the best base models score in the low single digits.

aime_2025.name: AIME 2025
aime_2025.description: American Invitational Mathematics Examination; 15-question, 3-hour exam with integer answers from 0 to 999, using the 2025 exam set.

aime_2026.name: AIME 2026
aime_2026.description: American Invitational Mathematics Examination; 15-question, 3-hour exam with integer answers from 0 to 999, using the 2026 exam set.

gpqa_diamond.name: GPQA Diamond
gpqa_diamond.description: Graduate-level Google-proof multiple-choice science questions (biology, physics, chemistry) from GPQA; Diamond split used in evals.

hle.name: Humanity's Last Exam
hle.description: Humanity's Last Exam: multi-modal benchmark with 2,500 expert-level questions across many subjects, designed to resist internet retrieval.

mmmu_pro.name: MMMU Pro
mmmu_pro.description: Vision-centric extension of MMMU that rigorously evaluates large multimodal models on challenging, college-level tasks requiring expert, cross‑disciplinary understanding and integrated visual–text reasoning.

osworld_verified.name: OSWorld-Verified
osworld_verified.description: Benchmark measuring GUI agents' ability to complete real computer tasks in a sandboxed Ubuntu environment; Foundation E2E GUI subset with max 100 steps, scored by task success rate.
